To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the naphthyl-urea-based compounds 5 and 10 show increased PSMA binding affinities compared to the parent compounds PSMA I&T and 68Ga-PSMA I& T, respectively.

the PSMA inhibitors with extended aromatic systems, such as biphenylalanines, show lower affinity to PSMA, whereas the urea-based PSMAS inhibitors with increased lipophility, e.g. naphthyl- and para-iodo-dL-phenylalanines, showed higher affinity and internalization.
the introduction of a 4-iodophenylalanine residue into the spacer of PSMA ligands increases plasma protein binding and enables sustained tumor uptake over 24 h.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the optimization of the pharmacokinetics of PSMA inhibitors by the introduction of lipophilic residues in the spacer region, which is a promising strategy to further improve PSMA-targeted radionuclide therapy.
the optimization of PSMA-targeted theranostics for prostate cancer treatment.
the development of PSMA inhibitors with improved pharmacokinetic properties, which may serve as a basis for the development of new theranostic tracers for prostate cancer therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the lipophilicity of PSMA inhibitors can be beneficially used in order to improve the tumor accumulation and retention, but also needs to be carefully considered and balanced to prevent renal retention.

the lipophilicity of urea-based ligands is an important parameter for the pharmacokinetic behavior and the biodistribution of PSMA-targeted compounds, and that a balance between lipophilicity and hydrophilicity needs to be achieved to optimize the tumor uptake and retention.
the increased lipophilicity of 10 and 17Lu-11 resulted in a higher PSMA affinity, internalization and tumor retention compared to the parent PSMA I&T compound.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a combination of a high affinity and a high lipophilicity of a PSMA-targeting agent can be beneficial to achieve high tumor uptake, but it can also lead to high renal uptake, especially in the presence of a low plasma protein binding.
the introduction of aromatic amino acids in PSMA ligands with the KuE motif as a pharmacophore is a promising strategy to improve the affinity and tumor uptake of PSMA inhibitors.
lipophilicity is an essential parameter to consider when designing PSMA inhibitors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the urea-based PSNA inhibitors can be optimized for both imaging and therapy, but further optimization is needed to improve the pharmacologic profile.
the lipophilicity of urea-based compounds can be increased by introduction of aromatic residues, without affecting the PSMA affinity.
the urea-based PS-MA inhibitor scaffold is highly adaptable and can be modified to improve affinity, internalization and plasma protein binding, and therefore tumor uptake and retention.
